answer: A trellis of sequential compute challenges binds each identity to a unique work path that cannot be parallelized. New agents must climb this trellis by solving a slow spiral of hashing rounds that grow harder with every additional account claimed from the same source, while an initial ember of burned tokens is required to start. An attacker forging many sybils pays both the rising compute time and the cumulative token burn for every fake identity, making large-scale attacks prohibitively expensive compared to honest single-identity participation.
